mcp_server_unrestricted.title: Hermes can control locks and doors
mcp_server_unrestricted.description:
The Model Context Protocol Server is not serving "{api_name}", so anything connected to it — including Hermes — gets the unrestricted Assist tools and can lock, unlock, open and close your doors.

To restrict it, open the Model Context Protocol Server integration, reconfigure it, and select "{api_name}".

Ignore this if you intend that client to have full control.

profile_ignored.title: Hermes is ignoring the profile name
profile_ignored.description:
Hermes is not routing on the profile prefix, so requests meant for "{profile}" are being served by the gateway's default profile instead. Nothing fails — the agent simply answers as the wrong persona.

Set `gateway.multiplex_profiles: true` in the Hermes gateway config and restart it. If you run a single-profile gateway on purpose, this warning is expected and can be ignored.

policy_unsupported.title: Hermes user group could not be created
policy_unsupported.description:
This Home Assistant version changed the internals this integration uses to create the "{group_name}" user group, so locks and doors are not protected by a user policy. The tool guard still applies on the restricted MCP API.

Until this integration is updated, you can create the group by hand in .storage/auth with Home Assistant stopped; see the README.

policy_user_admin.title: Hermes user is an administrator
policy_user_admin.description:
The user "{user_name}" chosen for Hermes is an administrator, so it cannot be placed in the restricted group and can control every entity, including locks.

Create a non-administrator user for Hermes and select it in the integration options.

policy_user_missing.title: Hermes user no longer exists
policy_user_missing.description: The Home Assistant user chosen for Hermes has been deleted. Select another user in the integration options, or choose "Not managed".

policy_user_groups.title: Hermes user belongs to other groups
policy_user_groups.description: The user "{user_name}" chosen for Hermes is a member of a group other than Users, so moving it into the restricted group would change what it may do. Choose a plain user in the integration options.

init.title: Hermes user
init.description: Choose the Home Assistant user Hermes signs in with. That user is moved into the "Hermes (locks and doors withheld)" group, which Home Assistant enforces on every route: MCP, the REST API, scripts and scenes. Choose "Not managed" to leave the user's groups alone.
